alex_k: Heads-up — nightly nsys run shows a regression on multi-GPU throughput after the recent kernel-selector change. Allreduce overlap is basically gone on gpuset-32. Timeline: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1962345678 :frowning:
perf-bot: Perf job 1962345678 finished • artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1962345678/ • nsys: s3://redwood-perf/1962345678/1962345678.nsys • perfetto: https://perf.redwood/1962345678/perfetto
maria: Which config (model / tp / batch)?
alex_k: gpt-medium, tp=2, pp=1, micro-batch=8 (client batch), baseline tokens/s ~1.9 -> now ~1.2. Suspect kernel launch reordering + an extra KV prefetch kernel getting scheduled before the collective.
jihoon: Can you paste the nsys command and a tiny timeline snippet?
alex_k: Run command:
```
nsys profile -o out_1962345678 -t cuda,osrt,nccl --stats=true \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace-fork-processes=true \
  python tools/run_inference.py --model gpt-medium --tp 2 --batch 8
```
nsys timeline excerpt (gpu wall time):
[GPU0] matmul_fwd (0.92ms) -> memcpy H2D (0.28ms) -> kernel_prefetch_kv (0.45ms) -> allreduce (6.5ms)   // gap before allreduce: 2.1ms
[GPU1] matmul_fwd (0.88ms) -> memcpy H2D (0.26ms) -> allreduce (1.2ms)                                    // overlapped
Comment: GPU0 has an extra kernel_prefetch_kv that pushes the collective later, killing overlap.
sam_t: That matches what I saw locally — the selector now prefers the new fused-gemm path for seq>512 which launches a small prefetch kernel on rank 0 before issuing NCCL. Commit: 8a7f6c3c broke launch ordering.
maria: Also check whether the KV handshake kernel uses stream0 vs a dedicated stream. If it's on stream0 it will serialize with the collective on that GPU.
alex_k: KV logs show prefetch on GPU0 at t=1203.5ms on stream0. I'll attach kv_prefetch.log to the ticket.
jihoon: Quick experiment suggestion: force legacy selector and reduce batch window to encourage batching. Env vars to try:
```
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy
export REDWOOD_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=2
```
Run with nvtx markers: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nccl --nvtx true -o test_legacy`.
alex_k: Ran that. Results: tokens/s -> 1.85, allreduce overlap restored across GPUs, gap reduced to ~0.2ms. Attached nsys: s3://redwood-perf/1962345678/legacy_run.nsys. So selector change is likely root cause.
perf-bot: Created PERF-4921: "kernel-selector: regression reduces NCCL overlap (tp=2, batch=8)" • assignee: alex_k • labels: [nccl, nsys, regression]
sam_t: Next actions: 1) revert selector change or add a gating flag; 2) add micro-benchmark asserting <20% regression on overlap for common seq lengths; 3) add NVTX markers around KV prefetch to ensure it doesn't run on stream0 when collectives are expected.
maria: I'll add an e2e perf CI job for tp=2 batch=8 and hook it to the PR blocking rule.
alex_k: I'll open a revert PR with perf traces and a brief reproduction script. Also will add nvtx markers in the selector code so we can inspect launch ordering during profiling. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sam_t: If anyone wants to reproduce quickly, use the docker image `gcr.io/redwood/perf:nightly-1962` and the `run_inference.py` args above.
alex_k: Filing a short postmortem into PERF-4921 after the revert PR lands.
